policy_title: Set Business Tax Stability and Reform Business Rates
stated: Labour will cap corporation tax at 25% for the entire parliament and maintain a permanent full expensing system for capital investment and the annual investment allowance for small businesses. They will replace the current business rates system in England with a new, fairer system that incentivises investment, tackles empty properties, and supports entrepreneurship.

source.quote: Labour will cap corporation tax at the current level of 25 per cent, the lowest in the G7, for the entire parliament, and we will act if tax changes in other countries pose a risk to UK competitiveness. We will retain a permanent full expensing system for capital investment and the annual investment allowance for small business. And we will give firms greater clarity on what qualifies for allowances to improve business investment decisions. The current business rates system disincentivises investment, creates uncertainty and places an undue burden on our high streets. In England, Labour will replace the business rates system, so we can raise the same revenue but in a fairer way. This new system will level the playing field between the high street and online giants, better incentivise investment, tackle empty properties and support entrepreneurship.

bearing_set.reason: Full expensing and the annual investment allowance directly incentivise capital investment, which drives productivity, job quality, and real wages; business rates reform affects small-business viability and hiring capacity.

Business rates are a direct operating cost for retail, hospitality, and high-street businesses; a fairer system that lowers those costs could reduce prices or prevent closures that sustain competition and consumer choice.

Full expensing and the annual investment allowance directly target capital investment and productivity; business rates reform targeting investment incentives and entrepreneurship directly affects firm formation and dynamism — all core O13 indicators.

Capping corporation tax at 25% for the full parliament removes the option to raise the main business tax rate if fiscal sustainability deteriorates, concretely constraining the debt-path management instrument in a period of limited OBR-assessed fiscal headroom.

membership_note: Primary bearing is on aggregate prosperity via investment incentives (O13); secondary bearing is the fiscal-flexibility cost of the CT ceiling (O12). Effects on wage distribution (O4), household prices (O2), and inequality (O14) are real debates but too indirect and mechanism-unspecified to clear the non-negligible bar as distinct verdicts here.
